newsitem.title: INDIA: India edible oil prices steady on imports,arrivals.
newsitem.headline: India edible oil prices steady on imports,arrivals.

text.p: Indian domestic edible oil prices remained steady during the past week on sustained imports and good summer crop arrivals, traders and industry officials said on Wednesday.
"Edible oil prices have stabilised after softening quite a bit," said Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd.
Traders said groundnut oil was quoted at 36,000 rupees per tonne compared with 36,000-36,500 rupees the previous week. Palm olein was traded at 27,000 rupees per tonne against 27,400 last week.
Industry officials said summer crop arrivals in all the states were completed except in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh and the western Gujarat state.
"Nearly 40,000 (70-kg) bags of groundnut in shell are arriving in the Saurashtra region per day," Shah said. The region is the main groundnut growing area in Gujarat state.
Sustained arrivals of imported edible oil had dragged prices to very low levels and they were not expected to fall further.
"About 5,000 tonnes to 10,000 tonnes of imported oil is arriving every week at the Bombay ports," Shah said.

He said about 175,000 tonnes of imported edible oil was expected to arrive in India in July and August. Since the beginning of the 1996/97 (November-October) season, India has contracted for more than 600,000 tonnes.

It imported about 1.25 million tonnes of edible oil in 1995/96 and industry officials expect imports to rise to about 1.5 million tonnes in the current season due to a rise in population and disposable income.
They said the forecast of a good monsoon in the 1997 season would marginally improve crop prospects for 1997/98.

"I expect the crop in 1997/98 to be about two or three percent higher on the prospects of a good monsoon," said O.P. Goenka, a senior official of the Central Organisation for the Oil Industry and Trade.
Industry officials expect the 1996/97 oilseeds crop to be about 21.26 million tonnes, up from 20.98 million in the previous season.
Summer output was expected to be about 9.35 million tonnes, down from 9.55 million.
India harvests two oilseeds crops annually, with the bulk of its output coming from the winter crop. The winter crop is sown in July and harvested from October.
